title: Cap. II Sol. Arg. 4: vas in honorem twofold — eternal purpose vs actual sanctification
pass_a_gloss: Add to this, that a vessel unto honour is said in two ways: Either from the eternal purpose of God electing unto honour: and so, that someone be a vessel unto honour does not depend on sanctification foreseen, but sanctification afterward flows from this decree. Or from actual sanctification: and in this sense someone then becomes a vessel unto honour, when purified and renewed by the Spirit of God he begins among the honoured servants of God to serve the Divine honour in holiness of life.
pass_b_english: Add: "vessel unto honour" is said two ways. From God's eternal electing purpose to honour — and then being such a vessel does not hang on foresight of sanctification; sanctification afterward flows from that decree. Or from actual sanctification — and in that sense someone becomes a vessel unto honour when, purified and renewed by God's Spirit, he begins among God's honoured servants to serve the divine honour in a holy life.
source_text: Huc adde, vas in honorem dupliciter dici: Vel ex proposito aeterno Dei eligentis ad honorem: & sic, ut quis sit vas in honorem, non pendet ex sanctificatione praevisa, sed sanctificatio postmodum fluit ab hoc decreto. Vel ex actuali sanctificatione: & hoc sensu tum fit aliquis vas in honorem, quando spiritu Dei purificatus & renovatus incipit inter honoratos Dei servos honori Divino in sanctitate vitae inservire.
